key_insight: GenEHR learns patient health trajectories from irregular EHR timelines and can be adapted to better forecast future cancer risk.
clinical_relevance: The model may help prioritize patients for risk-based screening and earlier attention to aggressive cancers such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.
method: Pretrained an autoregressive generative model on longitudinal electronic health records from millions of patients.
Explicitly modeled irregular time gaps between visits to predict future clinical events.
Applied parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for pan-cancer risk stratification.
evidence_signal: In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation improved prediction of first cancer diagnosis within a 5-year horizon.
watch_item: Retrospective performance must be validated prospectively before use as a clinical decision-support tool, especially to avoid overtriage or biased screening prioritization.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
